keyVerseText: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.
rootMeaning: The Greek verb παραφέρω (paraphérō) derives from the preposition παρά (pará), meaning 'beside' or 'near,' combined with φέρω (pherō), meaning 'to carry' or 'to bear.' This etymology conveys the idea of carrying or bringing something alongside or away from a certain place or position. Beyond the English glosses of 'remove' or 'take away,' the root sense emphasizes a movement that is not merely displacement but involves bearing something to the side or off from its original place, suggesting both literal and figurative carrying away or averting.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, παραφέρω is used sparingly, occurring only twice, yet it consistently carries the sense of removing or taking away. The top translations reflect this with 'take away' and 'remove,' indicating its primary function in the biblical text is to describe the act of carrying something off or averting it. This usage reveals a nuanced semantic range that includes both physical removal and metaphorical averting, broadening our understanding of how God or individuals may 'bear away' burdens or trials.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding παραφέρω enriches our grasp of divine intervention and human petition in Scripture, highlighting God's power to remove or carry away what burdens us. The concept of bearing something aside or away aligns with the biblical theme of God’s providential care, where He can avert suffering or remove obstacles according to His will. This verb underscores the dynamic relationship between human plea and divine sovereignty, reminding believers that God is able to carry away trials but always in accordance with His perfect purpose. It also points to Christ’s role in bearing away sin and judgment, a foundational truth for faith in His redemptive work.
keyVerseReflection: In Mark 14:36, Jesus prays, 'take away this cup from me,' using παραφέρω to express a desire for the removal or carrying away of impending suffering. The word conveys more than a mere wish; it reflects a plea for God to bear aside the burden, illustrating both Jesus’ humanity and submission to the Father’s will. This verb deepens the emotional and theological weight of the verse, showing that while Jesus sought relief, He ultimately entrusted Himself to God's sovereign plan, embodying perfect obedience and trust.
